idiom_name: java.util.ServiceLoader with Scala traits on the JVM (framework registries for host plugins)
implementation_notes: On the JVM a Scala trait compiles to an interface, so the JDK loader works unchanged: plugins implement the trait and are listed in META-INF/services, and the host enumerates them with ServiceLoader.load(classOf[Codec]) and can inspect provider types before instantiating. Scala.js has no ServiceLoader at all and Scala Native's load is a link-time intrinsic that only accepts a literal classOf, so on those platforms plugins are registered at link time by generated code rather than loaded - the JVM is the only Scala target that satisfies add-without-recompiling. Framework hosts add their own registry on top: Akka Extensions (an ExtensionId plus configuration-driven eager loading) are a plugin mechanism inside the ActorSystem, and sbt loads its build plugins the same way from declarative build files.
code_sketch:
trait Codec { def encode(doc: Document): Array[Byte] }

val providers = ServiceLoader.load(classOf[Codec])
val names = providers.stream().map(_.type().getName).toList   // no instantiation
val codec = providers.findFirst().orElseThrow()
providers.reload()
pitfalls: The context class loader trap applies unchanged (sbt, application servers and reloading engines reset it), so ServiceLoader.load can find nothing without any error being raised.

A Scala object provider is not instantiable by the loader (no public no-arg constructor; MODULE$ holds the instance), and trait fields or early initializers compile into constructor code, so provider construction semantics differ from Java.
In a cross-built project the same source may be compiled for JVM, JS and Native, where the META-INF/services file is silently ignored on the non-JVM platforms unless registration code is generated.
